title: Graph paper; calculator
subject: Geography
unit: Summer 1: Physical fieldwork enquiry (Paper 1 Section B)
source: Written for geography/y10 lesson 66 (Graph paper; calculator)
intro: Lesson 66: Presenting data: choosing and drawing the right graph. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.title: Sort into: Bar chart / Line graph / Scatter graph
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Bar chart, Line graph, Scatter graph.
blocks.answer: Bar chart: mean time per surface; run-off distance per surface. Line graph: river level over 3 days; rainfall each day. Scatter graph: slope angle vs infiltration time; plant cover vs infiltration time

model.title: Example data: flower bed trials 40 s, 52 s, 46 s

panels.title: A good graph
points: Title and labelled axes with units
Accurate plotting and a key if needed

keywords.def: bars showing amounts in separate categories
points showing the relationship between two variables
a line showing change over continuous time
a labelled line showing a scale
the total divided by the number of values

questions.q: Example data: compacted path trials 300 s, 280 s, 340 s. Mean?
Which graph for 'plant cover (%) against infiltration time'?

questions.a: A title, labelled axes with units and an even scale

questions.q: Core: Calculate the mean time for each surface from your data (or the example data), then draw a bar chart of means and one other suitable graph.
questions.a: Correct means; accurate, labelled bar chart and a second appropriate graph

questions.q: Extend: (3 marks, own exam-style) Justify your choice of graph for one data set.
questions.a: Names the data type, explains why the graph suits it, notes what it shows clearly

questions.q: Stretch: Why is a pie chart unsuitable for infiltration times?
questions.a: Times are not parts of a whole

questions.q: To show how river level changed over three days, use a:
questions.a: B) Line graph. Change over continuous time suits a line graph.

questions.q: Big question: why can a graph confuse?
questions.a: Wrong graph type, uneven scales or missing labels hide the pattern
